A second settings file would add a parallel read path beside the boundary that already owns this setting, so I am raising a framing concern before any other question.

A) as framed - add a second settings file that supplies the timeout override.
B) pivot: change the existing caller to pass its timeout override through `settings/resolver.ts` - this fixes the root cause on the one boundary every caller already uses (`settings/resolver.ts:11`), with no duplicate settings path.
C) smaller or none: document how to set the timeout through the existing resolver and ship no code change. If nothing ships, the override remains silently ignored for that caller.
Recommendation: B - the resolver already supports the override, so fixing the caller removes the bug without creating a second settings boundary.
